stem: Which of the following can claim compliance with the Global Investment Performance Standards?
options: An individual portfolio manager with a strong track record
A single mutual fund product, independent of its manager
An investment management firm that meets all applicable requirements
explanation: Compliance is claimed at the firm level and requires meeting all applicable requirements. Individuals and stand-alone products cannot claim compliance.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Individuals cannot claim compliance; only firms (and asset owners) can.
rationale.B: Incorrect. A product cannot be compliant on its own; compliance is a firm-wide claim.
rationale.C: Correct. A firm that meets every applicable requirement may claim compliance.

stem: The fictional Thornbury Capital wants to market its Emerging Markets Equity composite. One fee-paying, discretionary emerging markets account lost heavily last year, and the marketing team proposes leaving it out of the composite. Under GIPS, this proposal is:
options: Not permitted, because all fee-paying discretionary portfolios must be included in at least one composite
Permitted, if the firm discloses that one account was excluded
Permitted, because composites may be built from a firm's most representative accounts
explanation: Requiring every actual fee-paying discretionary portfolio to be in at least one composite prevents cherry-picking. A losing account that fits the strategy must be included.

rationale.A: Correct. Excluding the account would be cherry-picking, which composite rules are designed to prevent.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Disclosure does not cure the exclusion of an eligible portfolio; inclusion is required.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Composites are defined by strategy, not by which accounts look best.

stem: A composite at the fictional Pinecrest Advisors contains three portfolios. Portfolio X began the year at USD 40 million and returned 5%; Portfolio Y began at USD 35 million and returned 8%; Portfolio Z began at USD 25 million and returned -3%. Using beginning-of-period asset weights, the composite return is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 3.33% is the simple equal-weighted average (5 + 8 - 3)/3, which ignores portfolio size.
rationale.B: Correct. Asset-weighting the three returns gives 4.05%.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 6.40% results from dropping the losing Portfolio Z and weighting only X and Y, which is cherry-picking.

verify: const v=[40,35,25], r=[5,8,-3]; const t=v.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0); return v.reduce((s,x,i)=>s+x/t*r[i],0);

stem: The fictional Wexford Partners states in its marketing: "Wexford complies with GIPS for all composites except our real estate strategy, and our flagship composite has been verified." Which of the following is most accurate?
options: The claim is acceptable because the exception is clearly disclosed
The claim is acceptable because verification of the flagship composite substitutes for full compliance
The claim is not acceptable because compliance is all-or-nothing on a firm-wide basis
explanation: A firm cannot claim partial compliance. It must meet all applicable requirements firm-wide. Verification is also performed for the firm as a whole and does not substitute for compliance.

rationale.A: Incorrect. Disclosing an exception does not make a partial compliance claim acceptable.
rationale.B: Incorrect. Verification tests the firm's compliance; it is firm-wide and cannot replace meeting the requirements.
rationale.C: Correct. Compliance must be firm-wide and complete; "except" claims are not allowed.
